items.title: DNP3 Electric Substation Dissector (libsentinel_plugin_dnp3.so)
items.text: The DNP3 (Distributed Network Protocol) dissector inspects electric utility telecontrol and SCADA traffic on TCP/UDP port 20000. It parses Data Link, Transport, and Application layers to detect unauthorized Select-Before-Operate (SBO) relay tripping, class poll anomalies, and outstation address spoofing.

items.title: 2. Invariant Enforcement & Threat Signatures
items.text:
• Direct Operate Suppression: Industrial electrical safety standards mandate the use of Select-Before-Operate (FC 03 followed by FC 04) before tripping high-voltage switchgear. Issuing unexpected Direct Operate No Ack (FC 06) commands indicates automated grid sabotages (e.g., Industroyer2) and triggers an immediate in-kernel block.
  • CRC Validation: Evaluates the DNP3 Data Link CRC-16 polynomial (\(X^{16} + X^{13} + X^8 + 1\)) in hardware via AVX2 instructions.

items.title: EtherNet/IP & CIP Dissector (libsentinel_plugin_enip.so)
items.text: The EtherNet/IP dissector inspects Rockwell Automation (Allen-Bradley) control networks operating on TCP/UDP port 44818. It parses encapsulation headers and internal Common Industrial Protocol (CIP) commands, validating tag reads, tag writes, and assembly data integrity.

items.title: 2. Threat Vector: Unauthorized CIP Tag Writes
items.text:
Attackers exploit CIP by submitting unauthenticated Write Tag (Service 0x4D / 0x4E) requests to manipulate safety logic tags (e.g., EMERGENCY_STOP_BYPASS or PRESSURE_RELIEF_OVERRIDE).

libsentinel_plugin_enip.so parses symbolic CIP paths in memory and drops unauthorized mutations before the Rockwell ControlLogix controller updates its output table.

items.title: HART-IP Industrial Wireless Dissector (libsentinel_plugin_hart.so)
items.text: The HART-IP dissector monitors process automation networks, chemical refineries, and smart wireless instrumentation communicating over TCP/UDP port 5094. It decodes HART-IP protocol framing, token-passing PDU structures, and commands to detect transmitter calibration tampering.

items.title: 2. Detecting Physical Sensor Spoofing
items.text:
Adversaries targeting chemical plants often issue HART Command 45 (Trim DAC Zero) or Command 46 (Trim DAC Gain) to alter pressure and temperature sensor calibrations, making dangerous pressure buildups appear normal to plant operators. The dissector traps and drops unauthorized Command 45/46 requests at the perimeter.

items.title: Modbus TCP Dissector Plugin (libsentinel_plugin_modbus.so)
items.text: The Modbus TCP dissector inspects industrial Modbus Application Protocol Data Units (APDU) on TCP port 502. It identifies unauthorized PLC function codes, illegal coil overrides, register range tampering, and high-frequency polling floods.

items.title: 2. In-Place Dissection Implementation (ModbusDissector.cpp)
items.text:
#include <sentinel/dissector_interface.hpp>
#include <arpa/inet.h>
#include <cstring>

namespace sentinel::plugins {

#pragma pack(push, 1)
struct MbapHeader {
    uint16_t transaction_id;
    uint16_t protocol_id; // Must be 0x0000 for Modbus TCP
    uint16_t length;
    uint8_t  unit_id;
};
#pragma pack(pop)

class ModbusDissector final : public IDissectorPlugin {
public:
    std::string_view protocol_name() const noexcept override { return "MODBUS_TCP"; }
    uint16_t default_port() const noexcept override { return 502; }
    uint32_t dissector_id() const noexcept override { return 101; }

    DissectionResult dissect(std::span<const uint8_t> payload, uint64_t timestamp_ns) noexcept override {
        DissectionResult res{};
        if (payload.size() < sizeof(MbapHeader) + 1) {
            return res; // Truncated frame
        }

        const auto* mbap = reinterpret_cast<const MbapHeader*>(payload.data());
        if (ntohs(mbap->protocol_id) != 0) {
            return res; // Not Modbus protocol
        }

        res.is_protocol_match = true;
        uint8_t function_code = payload[sizeof(MbapHeader)];

        // Trap unauthorized Diagnostic Function Codes (Common in reconnaissance)
        if (function_code == 0x08 || function_code == 0x2B) {
            res.is_anomaly_detected = true;
            res.rule_id = 1801;
            res.severity = 3;
            std::strncpy(res.description, "Unauthorized Modbus Diagnostic/Encapsulated Command", 63);
            return res;
        }

        // Validate Write Operations (FC 05, 06, 15, 16)
        if (function_code == 16 && payload.size() >= sizeof(MbapHeader) + 5) {
            uint16_t start_reg = ntohs(*reinterpret_cast<const uint16_t*>(payload.data() + sizeof(MbapHeader) + 1));
            // Enforce protected register zone: Addresses 40001 - 40050 are safety-critical
            if (start_reg < 50) {
                res.is_anomaly_detected = true;
                res.rule_id = 1802;
                res.severity = 4; // Critical
                std::strncpy(res.description, "Safety-Critical PLC Register Mutation Attempt", 63);
            }
        }

        return res;
    }
};

} // namespace sentinel::plugins

#include <cstdint>

namespace sentinel::subsystems {

struct ActuatorWearTracker {
    uint32_t register_id{0};
    uint64_t total_cycles{0};
    uint64_t max_duty_cycles_per_hour{100};
    uint64_t cycles_this_hour{0};
    uint64_t last_cycle_time_ns{0};

    bool record_actuation(uint64_t now_ns) noexcept {
        // Enforce minimum physical refractory period (e.g. 500ms between valve shifts)

        last_cycle_time_ns = now_ns;
        total_cycles++;
        cycles_this_hour++;
        return cycles_this_hour <= max_duty_cycles_per_hour;
    }
};

items.text:
#pragma once

#include <array>
#include <string_view>
#include <cstdint>
#include <vector>
#include <shared_mutex>

namespace sentinel::subsystems {

struct SiemRecord {
    uint64_t timestamp_ns{0};
    uint32_t src_ipv4{0};
    uint32_t dst_ipv4{0};
    uint16_t subsystem_id{0};
    uint16_t rule_id{0};
    uint8_t severity{0}; // 0 = Info, 1 = Low, 2 = Medium, 3 = High, 4 = Critical
    char description[64]{0};
};

class SiemCore {
public:
    static constexpr size_t RING_CAPACITY = 1048576; // 1M events

    void ingest(const SiemRecord& record) noexcept {
        uint64_t idx = write_cursor_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
        size_t slot = idx & (RING_CAPACITY - 1);
        ring_[slot] = record;
        update_indices(slot, record);
    }

    // Query records matching an IP address in under 5 milliseconds
    std::vector<SiemRecord> query_by_ip(uint32_t ip, size_t limit = 100) const {
        std::shared_lock lock(index_mutex_);
        std::vector<SiemRecord> results;
        results.reserve(limit);

        auto it = ip_index_.find(ip);
        if (it != ip_index_.end()) {
            for (size_t slot : it->second) {
                results.push_back(ring_[slot]);
                if (results.size() >= limit) break;
            }
        }
        return results;
    }

private:
    std::array<SiemRecord, RING_CAPACITY> ring_{};
    std::atomic<uint64_t> write_cursor_{0};
    mutable std::shared_mutex index_mutex_;
    std::unordered_map<uint32_t, std::vector<size_t>> ip_index_;

    void update_indices(size_t slot, const SiemRecord& rec);
};

} // namespace sentinel::subsystems

items.title: Subsystem 02: User & Entity Behavior Analytics (02_ueba)
items.text: 02_ueba models baseline operational profiles for up to 100,000 network entities (users, IP addresses, service accounts, and PLC nodes). It detects credential stuffing, insider threats, privilege escalation, and beaconing behavior by computing deviations from rolling statistical baselines.

items.title: 1. The 100,000-Entity State Matrix
items.text:
To prevent dynamic heap allocation, 02_ueba uses a statically pre-allocated state matrix:

 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ 100k-Entity State Matrix (Fixed 256 MB Static Allocation)   │
 └──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                                │ Hash(Entity ID) & (131072 - 1)
                                ▼
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ EntitySlot [131,072 Buckets]                                │
 │  - Baseline Moving Average (Packets, Bytes, Flow Durations) │
 │  - First-Order Markov Chain (State Transition Matrix)       │
 │  - Activity Time Histogram (24-Hour Binned Array)           │
 │  - Cumulative Risk Score (0.0 to 100.0)                     │
 └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

items.title: 2. Statistical Baseline & Markov Transition Model
items.text:
The subsystem calculates anomaly probabilities using a combined metric score:

\[\text{Risk}(E) = w_1 \cdot \frac{|X_{\text{observed}} - \mu_{\text{baseline}}|}{\sigma_{\text{baseline}}} + w_2 \cdot \left(1.0 - P_{\text{Markov}}(S_t \mid S_{t-1})\right)\]

Where: * \(\frac{|X - \mu|}{\sigma}\) represents the Z-score deviation of connection frequencies or byte volumes. * \(P_{\text{Markov}}(S_t \mid S_{t-1})\) measures the probability of moving from protocol state \(S_{t-1}\) (e.g., SMB Read) to state \(S_t\) (e.g., Active Directory DCSync) based on historical entity habits.

items.title: 2. In-Memory JA3 Vectorizer (NdrEngine.cpp)
items.text:
#include <string>
#include <openssl/md5.h>
#include <span>

namespace sentinel::subsystems {

struct TlsClientHelloInfo {
    uint16_t client_version;
    std::vector<uint16_t> cipher_suites;
    std::vector<uint16_t> extensions;
    std::vector<uint16_t> supported_groups;
    std::vector<uint8_t> ec_point_formats;
};

std::string compute_ja3_hash(const TlsClientHelloInfo& hello) {
    std::string raw;
    raw.reserve(256);

    raw += std::to_string(hello.client_version) + ",";

    // Append ciphers
    for (size_t i = 0; i < hello.cipher_suites.size(); ++i) {
        raw += std::to_string(hello.cipher_suites[i]);
        if (i + 1 < hello.cipher_suites.size()) raw += "-";
    }
    raw += ",";

    // Append extensions...
    // (MD5 hash executed over pre-allocated buffer)
    unsigned char digest[MD5_DIGEST_LENGTH];
    MD5(reinterpret_cast<const unsigned char*>(raw.data()), raw.size(), digest);

    char hex_str[33];
    for (int i = 0; i < 16; ++i) {
        snprintf(&(hex_str[i * 2]), 3, "%02x", digest[i]);
    }
    return std::string(hex_str, 32);
}

} // namespace sentinel::subsystems

items.title: 2. High-Frequency Rate Limiting via Token Buckets
items.text:
13_ddos maintains an in-kernel per-IP token bucket map:

struct token_bucket {
    __u64 last_update_ns;
    __u64 tokens;
};

// Returns 1 if permitted, 0 if rate limit exceeded (Trigger XDP_DROP)
static __always_inline int check_rate_limit(struct token_bucket *b, __u64 rate, __u64 capacity) {
    __u64 now = bpf_ktime_get_ns();
    __u64 elapsed = now - b->last_update_ns;
    b->last_update_ns = now;

    // Replenish tokens based on elapsed nanoseconds
    b->tokens += (elapsed * rate) / 1000000000ULL;
    if (b->tokens > capacity) b->tokens = capacity;

    if (b->tokens > 0) {
        b->tokens--;
        return 1; // Allow packet
    }
    return 0; // Rate limit breach -> DROP
}

#include <fstream>
#include <vector>
#include <cstdint>

namespace sentinel::subsystems {

#pragma pack(push, 1)
struct PcapGlobalHeader {
    uint32_t magic_number{0xa1b2c3d4};
    uint16_t version_major{2};
    uint16_t version_minor{4};
    int32_t  thiszone{0};
    uint32_t sigfigs{0};
    uint32_t snaplen{65535};
    uint32_t network{1}; // LINKTYPE_ETHERNET
};

struct PcapPacketHeader {
    uint32_t ts_sec;
    uint32_t ts_usec;
    uint32_t incl_len;
    uint32_t orig_len;
};
#pragma pack(pop)

void flush_carved_pcap(const std::string& path, const std::vector<uint8_t>& raw_frames) {
    std::ofstream out(path, std::ios::binary);
    PcapGlobalHeader gh;
    out.write(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(&gh), sizeof(gh));
    out.write(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(raw_frames.data()), raw_frames.size());
}

} // namespace sentinel::subsystems

items.title: 2. Netlink Process Connector Interface (EdrEngine.cpp)
items.text:
#include <linux/netlink.h>
#include <linux/connector.h>
#include <linux/cn_proc.h>
#include <sys/socket.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <iostream>

namespace sentinel::subsystems {

class EdrEngine {
public:
    void init_netlink_listener() {
        nl_sock_ = ::socket(PF_NETLINK, SOCK_DGRAM | SOCK_CLOEXEC, NETLINK_CONNECTOR);
        if (nl_sock_ < 0) {
            throw std::runtime_error("Failed to open Netlink process connector socket");
        }

        struct sockaddr_nl sa{};
        sa.nl_family = AF_NETLINK;
        sa.nl_groups = CN_IDX_PROC;
        sa.nl_pid = getpid();

        if (::bind(nl_sock_, reinterpret_cast<struct sockaddr*>(&sa), sizeof(sa)) < 0) {
            ::close(nl_sock_);
            throw std::runtime_error("Failed to bind Netlink socket");
        }

        // Subscribe to process events
        subscribe_proc_events(true);
    }

    void process_event(const struct proc_event& ev) {
        switch (ev.what) {
            case PROC_EVENT_EXEC:
                evaluate_exec_anomaly(ev.event_data.exec.process_pid, ev.event_data.exec.process_tgid);
                break;
            case PROC_EVENT_PTRACE:
                flag_memory_tampering(ev.event_data.ptrace.process_pid, ev.event_data.ptrace.tracer_pid);
                break;
            default:
                break;
        }
    }

private:
    int nl_sock_{-1};
    void subscribe_proc_events(bool enable);
    void evaluate_exec_anomaly(pid_t pid, pid_t tgid);
    void flag_memory_tampering(pid_t target, pid_t tracer);
};

} // namespace sentinel::subsystems

items.text: 07_epp_ngav defends edge storage from ransomware and wiper attacks. items.title: 1. Shannon Entropy Formula & SIMD Acceleration
items.text:
Encrypted files (ransomware ciphertext) and packed binaries display near-uniform byte frequency distributions, pushing entropy toward \(8.0\):

\[H(X) = -\sum_{i=0}^{255} P(x_i) \log_2 P(x_i)\] 
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ Byte Frequency Histogram (256-Element Integer Array)        │
 └──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                                │ Vectorized AVX2 / ARM Neon
                                ▼
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ Shannon Entropy Classification:                             │
 │  • Plaintext / Source Code:     1.5 to 4.2 bits/byte        │
 │  • Compiled Native Binaries:    5.0 to 6.4 bits/byte        │
 │  • Ransomware Ciphertext:       7.85 to 8.00 bits/byte      │
 └──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                                │
                                ▼ Rapid Shift (> 7.85 on > 10 files/sec)

items.title: 2. In-Memory Entropy Calculation (EntropyCalculator.cpp)
items.text:
#include <immintrin.h>
#include <cmath>
#include <span>
#include <array>

namespace sentinel::subsystems {

double calculate_shannon_entropy(std::span<const uint8_t> buffer) noexcept {
    if (buffer.empty()) return 0.0;

    std::array<uint32_t, 256> counts{};
    for (uint8_t byte : buffer) {
        counts[byte]++;
    }

    const double total = static_cast<double>(buffer.size());
    double entropy = 0.0;

    for (uint32_t count : counts) {
        if (count > 0) {
            double p = static_cast<double>(count) / total;
            entropy -= p * std::log2(p);
        }
    }
    return entropy;
}

} // namespace sentinel::subsystems

items.title: In-Kernel eBPF Driver Attachment Issues
items.text: This guide resolves network interface binding failures and eBPF hook rejections across physical and virtual network adapters.

items.title: Symptom
items.text: [FATAL] XdpManager: Failed to attach xdp_filter.o to interface ens33 in DRIVER mode: Operation not supported (errno 95)

items.title: Causes & Remediation
items.text:
1. Conflicting Hardware Offloads: The VMware vmxnet3 driver blocks native XDP if Large Receive Offload (LRO) or Generic Receive Offload (GRO) is active. Disable them via ethtool: 
    sudo ethtool -K ens33 lro off gro off rxvlan off txvlan off
  2. MTU Exceeds Driver Page Bounds: If MTU is greater than 1500, native XDP allocation will fail: 
    sudo ip link set dev ens33 mtu 1500
  3. Fallback to Generic SKB Mode: If native driver mode remains unsupported on legacy virtual hardware, switch the operational mode in /etc/sentinel/sentinel.yaml: 
    network:
  xdp_attach_mode: "SKB"

items.title: Symptom
items.text: [ERROR] XdpManager: Interface eth0 already has an active XDP program attached.

items.title: Remediation
items.text:
Force-clear any orphaned or crashed XDP programs:

sudo ip link set dev eth0 xdp off
sudo ip link set dev eth0 xdpgeneric off

Then restart sentinel:

sudo systemctl restart sentinel

items.title: Q1: Does blackbox-sentinel require an active internet connection?
items.text: No. blackbox-sentinel is designed for sovereign, air-gapped deployments. All 26 subsystems, 30 protocol dissectors, and local SIEM indexing engines execute 100% on-premises with $0.00 cloud data egress. It functions indefinitely without external DNS or internet access.

items.title: Q2: What happens if the central sentinel-nexus hub goes down?
items.text: The edge appliance operates with full local autonomy: * In-kernel packet mitigation (\(< 0.84\,\mu\text{s}\)) continues uninterrupted. * Local SIEM log correlation and web command center management remain operational. * Emitted telemetry and forensic PCAP files are buffered in local circular memory until the Nexus connection is restored.

items.title: Q3: How does the appliance maintain \(< 0.84\,\mu\text{s}\) drops under heavy network loads?
items.text: The mitigation fast-path runs inside the network interface card (NIC) driver space using Linux eBPF/XDP. When an incoming frame matches an active threat rule, the kernel returns XDP_DROP and recycles the hardware descriptor immediately, avoiding the CPU and memory costs of allocating Linux sk_buff socket buffers.

items.title: Q4: Can I run third-party security agents (e.g., Splunk, CrowdStrike) alongside sentinel?
items.text: Yes. blackbox-sentinel integrates with existing enterprise infrastructure. It exposes industry-standard log forwarders (CEF, LEEF, Syslog RFC 5424, and Kafka) to stream enriched security telemetry to central SIEMs without system conflicts.

items.title: Nexus Fleet Uplink Disconnection Diagnostics
items.text: This guide covers troubleshooting network drops, mTLS handshake rejections, and gRPC timeouts between blackbox-sentinel and sentinel-nexus.

items.title: Symptom
items.text: [WARN] NexusUplink: gRPC connection to 10.240.0.10:50051 failed: 14: Socket failed to connect to all addresses

items.title: Diagnosis Checklist
items.text:
1. Network Connectivity: Test TCP layer reachability to port 50051: 
    nc -zv 10.240.0.10 50051
  2. Firewall Blocking: Ensure intermediate firewalls allow bidirectional traffic over TCP port 50051.
  3. Hub Service Health: Verify that the sentinel-nexus daemon is running on the central server: 
    sudo systemctl status sentinel-nexus

items.title: Symptom
items.text: [ERROR] NexusUplink: mTLS Handshake failed: 16: SSL_ERROR_SSL: certificate verify failed

items.title: Causes & Fixes
items.text:
1. Clock Drift: If the appliance system time deviates by more than \(300\text{ seconds}\) from the Nexus hub, certificate validity checks will fail. Synchronize clocks via NTP: 
    sudo chronyc makestep
  2. Expired Client Certificate: Check the expiration timestamp of /etc/sentinel/certs/appliance.crt: 
    openssl x509 -in /etc/sentinel/certs/appliance.crt -noout -enddate
    If expired, re-run the hardware enrollment handshake to obtain an updated signed certificate lease.

items.title: Protocol Dissector & Plugin Loading Failures
items.text: blackbox-sentinel loads its 30 industrial protocol dissectors dynamically from /usr/local/lib/sentinel-plugins/. This guide resolves dynamic linker and ABI compatibility issues.

items.title: Symptom
items.text: [ERROR] PluginManager: Failed to load libsentinel_plugin_modbus.so: libmodbus.so.5: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory

items.title: Remediation
items.text:
1. Verify that all runtime dependency libraries are installed on the host: 
    ldd /usr/local/lib/sentinel-plugins/libsentinel_plugin_modbus.so
  2. Update the dynamic linker cache: 
    sudo ldconfig
  3. If dependencies reside in non-standard directories, update /etc/ld.so.conf.d/sentinel.conf or specify: 
    export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib/sentinel-deps:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH

items.title: Symptom

items.title: Cause
items.text: The dissector shared object was compiled against an outdated header definition of IDissectorPlugin.hpp.

items.title: Remediation
items.text:
Recompile the plugin modules using the unified sentinel-stack installer:

cd /opt/sentinel-stack
sudo ./install.sh --rebuild-plugins

items.title: Startup Failures & Configuration Diagnostics
items.text: This guide provides troubleshooting and remediation steps for daemon startup aborts, configuration parser errors, and file permission issues in blackbox-sentinel.

items.title: 1. YAML Parser Failures & Inline Comment Bugs
Symptom
items.text:
[FATAL] ConfigManager: Failed to parse /etc/sentinel/sentinel.yaml: bad conversion on line 14: '8443 # Port'
[FATAL] Uvicorn/REST: 400 Bad Request: Invalid HTTP request received

items.title: Cause
items.text: Earlier versions of custom YAML parsers read inline comments (# ...) as part of the string or numeric literal, resulting in invalid port numbers or whitespace-corrupted endpoints.

items.title: Remediation
items.text:
1. Verify that blackbox-sentinel is updated to the latest build, which implements automated comment stripping before type coercion in ConfigManager.cpp.
  2. Ensure clean separation between values and comments in /etc/sentinel/sentinel.yaml: 
    # Correct formatting:
web_console:
  port: 8443
  3. Run the configuration validation tool: 
    sentinel --validate-config /etc/sentinel/sentinel.yaml

items.title: Symptom
items.text:
[FATAL] ConfigManager: Missing mandatory section 'ai_runtime' or 'network'
[FATAL] ApplianceCore initialization aborted with error code -10

items.title: Remediation
items.text: Ensure /etc/sentinel/sentinel.yaml includes all seven root configuration sections: * appliance * network * ai_runtime * hardware_identity * web_console * nexus_uplink * storage

items.title: Symptom
items.text: [ERROR] WebConsole: Could not load private key from /etc/sentinel/certs/server.key: Permission denied

items.title: Remediation
items.text:
Ensure certificate files are readable by the executing service user or group:

sudo chown root:sentinel /etc/sentinel/certs/server.key
sudo chmod 640 /etc/sentinel/certs/server.key

items.title: 1. Automated Diagnostic Bundle Generation

sudo sentinel --diag-bundle --output /tmp/sentinel_diagnostic_bundle.tar.gz

items.title: Preventing Container Breakouts with eBPF CWPP (09_cwpp)
items.text: This tutorial demonstrates how Subsystem 09_cwpp intercepts container escapes and namespace privilege escalation attempts in Docker and Kubernetes clusters by tracking syscalls at tracepoint:raw_syscalls:sys_enter.
path: Preventing Container Breakouts with eBPF CWPP (`09_cwpp`)

items.title: 1. Attack Scenario: Host Filesystem Mount Escape
items.text:
An attacker compromises an unprivileged container running a vulnerable web application and attempts to break out of the container namespace by mounting the host's root block device (/dev/sda1):

# Attacker command inside compromised container
mkdir /mnt/host && mount /dev/sda1 /mnt/host
path: Preventing Container Breakouts with eBPF CWPP (`09_cwpp`)

items.title: 2. Enabling Subsystem 09_cwpp
items.text:
Ensure 09_cwpp is enabled in /etc/sentinel/sentinel.yaml:

subsystems:
  cwpp:
    enabled: true
    monitor_container_namespaces: true
    trap_host_mount_escapes: true
    trap_unshare_privilege_escalation: true
    trap_cgroup_release_agent: true
    action: "TERMINATE_CONTAINER_PROCESS"
path: Preventing Container Breakouts with eBPF CWPP (`09_cwpp`)

items.title: 3. Executing the Test Inside Docker
items.text:
Launch an isolated test container:

docker run --rm -it --cap-add=SYS_ADMIN alpine sh

Inside the container shell, attempt the mount breakout:

mkdir /tmp/escape && mount /dev/sda1 /tmp/escape
path: Preventing Container Breakouts with eBPF CWPP (`09_cwpp`)

items.title: Observation & Result
items.text:
The mount syscall is intercepted in kernel space by cwpp_guard.bpf.c: 1. The kernel tracepoint returns -EPERM (Operation not permitted). 2. 09_cwpp sends an immediate SIGKILL to the offending process PID inside the container. 3. The containerized shell terminates with:

Killed
path: Preventing Container Breakouts with eBPF CWPP (`09_cwpp`)

items.title: Sentinel Appliance Log
items.text:
[CWPP ALERT] Container Escape Attempt Intercepted:
    Container ID : c8f2b3e104a1
    Syscall      : __NR_mount (165)
    Target Device: /dev/sda1 -> /tmp/escape
    Action       : Syscall neutralized with -EPERM; PID 18402 terminated via SIGKILL.
path: Preventing Container Breakouts with eBPF CWPP (`09_cwpp`)

items.title: Deploying a 15-Minute Non-Intrusive SPAN Shadow Audit
items.text: This tutorial demonstrates how to deploy blackbox-sentinel in a completely passive, zero-risk evaluation mode using an industrial network switch mirror port (SPAN). In this configuration, the appliance observes and scores live traffic without modifying network packets or dropping flows.
path: Deploying a 15-Minute Non-Intrusive SPAN Shadow Audit

items.title: 1. Network Topology: Passive Mirroring
items.text:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ Industrial Managed Switch (e.g. Hirschmann / Cisco IE3400)  │
 ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │ Port 1: SCADA HMI Host      ──► Port 2: Siemens S7-1500 PLC │
 │ Port 8 (SPAN / Mirror Port) : Copies 100% of Port 1 & 2 Rx/Tx│
 └──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                                │ Physical Patch Cable
                                ▼
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ Blackbox-Sentinel Appliance (Interface: eth1)               │
 │  - Deployment Stage: STAGE_SHADOW_MODE                      │
 │  - Evaluates traffic through all 26 subsystems in RAM       │
 │  - eBPF Filter returns XDP_PASS ONLY (Zero Packet Drops)    │
 │  - Real-Time Web Console active on eth0 (Port 8443 HTTPS)   │
 └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
path: Deploying a 15-Minute Non-Intrusive SPAN Shadow Audit

items.title: 2. Appliance Configuration (/etc/sentinel/sentinel.yaml)
items.text:
Configure eth1 as the passive sniffing interface and set the operational stage to STAGE_SHADOW_MODE:

version: "1.0.0"

appliance:
  node_name: "substation-shadow-auditor"
  deployment_stage: "STAGE_SHADOW_MODE" # Enforces zero packet drops
  log_level: "INFO"

network:
  primary_interface: "eth1"
  promiscuous_mode: true
  xdp_attach_mode: "DRIVER" # Native driver mode for wire-speed parsing
  bpf_filter_path: "/usr/local/lib/bpf/xdp_filter.o"

web_console:
  enabled: true
  bind_address: "192.168.1.100" # Management interface IP (eth0)
  port: 8443
path: Deploying a 15-Minute Non-Intrusive SPAN Shadow Audit

items.title: 3. Deployment Steps
items.text:
# 1. Bring up the SPAN interface in promiscuous mode
sudo ip link set dev eth1 promisc on up

# 2. Validate configuration
sentinel --validate-config /etc/sentinel/sentinel.yaml

# 3. Start the daemon under systemd
sudo systemctl restart sentinel
path: Deploying a 15-Minute Non-Intrusive SPAN Shadow Audit

items.title: 4. Inspecting Audit Results
items.text:
Open your browser and navigate to https://192.168.1.100:8443.

During the 14-day audit window, the dashboard presents: * Full asset discovery across Modbus, S7, DNP3, and IEC 104 devices. * Behavioral baseline deviations recorded by Subsystem 02_ueba. * Physical invariant warnings flagged by Subsystem 18_cps_sec. * Comprehensive compliance gap analysis exportable as an audit PDF.
path: Deploying a 15-Minute Non-Intrusive SPAN Shadow Audit

items.title: Inline Active Protection for Industrial PLCs (Modbus & Siemens S7)
items.text: This tutorial guides you through placing blackbox-sentinel inline as a transparent active defense bridge between an engineering workstation and a Schneider Modicon M340 / Siemens S7 PLC, enforcing sub-microsecond in-kernel drops against unauthorized register mutations.
path: Inline Active Protection for Industrial PLCs (Modbus & Siemens S7)

items.title: 1. Inline Physical Bridge Architecture
items.text:
[ SCADA Engineering Workstation ]
                │
                ▼ Ingress Cable
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ Blackbox-Sentinel Hardware Appliance (Inline Bridge)        │
 │  - Ingress: eth1 | Egress: eth2                             │

items.title: 2. Invariant Rules Configuration
items.text:
Edit /etc/sentinel/sentinel.yaml to enforce strict boundaries on critical centrifuge registers:

appliance:
  node_name: "substation-active-guard"
  deployment_stage: "STAGE_FULL_ACTIVE" # Enforces automated in-kernel drops

network:
  primary_interface: "eth1"
  xdp_attach_mode: "DRIVER"

subsystems:
  cps_sec:
    enabled: true
    enforce_physical_invariants: true
    industrial_invariants:
      - rule_id: 1801
        description: "Centrifuge Motor Speed Bounds"
        protocol: "MODBUS_TCP"
        unit_id: 1
        target_register: 40010
        valid_range:
          min: 500   # Minimum 500 RPM
          max: 3600  # Maximum 3600 RPM (Over-speed runaway protection)
        max_rate_of_change:
          max_delta_per_second: 300 # Traps instantaneous acceleration commands
        violation_ttl_seconds: 300

Restart the appliance:

sudo systemctl restart sentinel
path: Inline Active Protection for Industrial PLCs (Modbus & Siemens S7)

items.title: Securing a Hospital PACS Radiology Enclave from Exfiltration
items.text:
Medical imaging environments running Picture Archiving and Communication Systems (PACS) often communicate over unencrypted DICOM streams.

This tutorial walks through deploying blackbox-sentinel to protect a hospital radiology enclave from unauthorized DICOM C-MOVE mass exfiltration and ransomware payload injection.
path: Securing a Hospital PACS Radiology Enclave from Exfiltration

items.title: 1. Network Placement
path: Securing a Hospital PACS Radiology Enclave from Exfiltration

items.title: 2. Configuring DICOM Protection Rules
items.text:
Configure Subsystem 17_iot_sec in /etc/sentinel/sentinel.yaml:

subsystems:
  iot_sec:
    enabled: true
    dicom_protection:
      enforce_aet_whitelist: true
      authorized_calling_aets:
        - "CT_SCANNER_01"
        - "MRI_SIEMENS_02"
        - "PACS_CENTRAL_SRV"
      max_c_move_queries_per_minute: 20 # Traps automated bulk exfiltration
      block_unknown_transfer_syntax: true # Drops non-standard executable payloads
      violation_action: "KERNEL_DROP"
      violation_ttl_seconds: 600
path: Securing a Hospital PACS Radiology Enclave from Exfiltration

items.title: 3. Testing with dcmtk Tools
items.text:
Simulate an unauthorized client attempting a bulk record harvest using the movescu utility:

# Querying records using an unregistered AE Title
movescu -v -aet UNKNOWN_RESEARCH -aec PACS_CENTRAL_SRV 10.240.0.100 104 -k PatientName="*"
path: Securing a Hospital PACS Radiology Enclave from Exfiltration

items.title: Result
items.text:
The initial A-ASSOCIATE-RQ packet is parsed in memory. Because UNKNOWN_RESEARCH is not whitelisted, 17_iot_sec commands Tier 2 libblackbox to block the attacker's IP:

    Source IP    : 10.240.0.88
    Calling AET  : UNKNOWN_RESEARCH (Unauthorized)
    Operation    : Bulk Patient Query (C-MOVE)
    Mitigation   : Source IP blocked in kernel for 600s. Exfiltration neutralized.
path: Securing a Hospital PACS Radiology Enclave from Exfiltration

items.title: Real-Time Telemetry Streaming & Dashboard Architecture
items.text: The Web Command Center renders real-time telemetry updates using Server-Sent Events (SSE) over /api/v1/telemetry/stream, streaming metrics directly from the in-memory ring buffers to the browser without polling overhead.

items.title: 2. Server-Sent Events (SSE) Dispatcher (WebTelemetryStream.cpp)
items.text:
#include <string>
#include <sstream>
#include <blackbox/telemetry.hpp>

namespace sentinel::web {

std::string serialize_sse_telemetry(
    const blackbox::KernelTelemetry& kernel, 
    double cpu_usage, 
    double npu_temp
) {
    std::ostringstream ss;
    ss << "event: telemetry_tick\n"
       << "data: {"
       << "\"timestamp_ns\":" << get_monotonic_ns() << ","
       << "\"cpu_ingress_percent\":" << cpu_usage << ","
       << "\"npu_temperature_c\":" << npu_temp << ","
       << "\"packets_processed\":" << kernel.total_packets_processed << ","
       << "\"packets_dropped\":" << kernel.total_packets_dropped << ","
       << "\"active_rules\":" << kernel.active_blocked_ips << ","
       << "\"drop_rate_pct\":" << kernel.drop_rate_percentage
       << "}\n\n";

    return ss.str();
}

} // namespace sentinel::web

items.title: In-Kernel eBPF Drop Table Management
items.text: The Web Command Center provides administrators with direct visibility into the active in-kernel blocked_ip_map, allowing operators to monitor automated mitigations, inspect remaining TTL durations, and execute 1-click manual unblocks.

items.title: 2. The 1-Click Unblock API Flow
items.text:
When an administrator clicks [UNBLOCK]:

 Operator Clicks [UNBLOCK] in Web Dashboard
                   │
                   ▼ HTTP POST /api/v1/drops/unblock
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ Web API Handler validates JWT Bearer Authorization Token    │
 └─────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────┘
                   │ Invokes blackbox::XdpManager::unblock_ip()
                   ▼
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ Linux Kernel: BPF_MAP_DELETE_ELEM Syscall                   │
 │   - Map: /sys/fs/bpf/blackbox/blocked_ip_map                │
 │   - Execution Latency: ~140 nanoseconds                     │
 └─────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────┘
                   │
                   ▼
 [ Source IP unblocked immediately; subsequent packets pass ]

items.title: 3. C++ Unblock Handler Implementation
items.text:
void handle_unblock_request(const HttpRequest& req, HttpResponse& resp, blackbox::XdpManager& xdp) {
    if (!validate_jwt_admin_claim(req.get_header("Authorization"))) {
        resp.set_status(401, "Unauthorized");
        return;
    }

    uint32_t ip = parse_ipv4_param(req.json()["ipv4"].get<std::string>());

    // Direct kernel syscall to remove entry from BPF map
    xdp.unblock_ip(ip);

    resp.set_status(200, "OK");
    resp.set_json({{"status", "UNBLOCKED"}, {"ipv4_net", ip}});
}

items.title: Real-Time Explainable AI (XAI) Feature Attribution Viewer
items.text:
Traditional Deep Learning models operate as opaque "black boxes," making it difficult for plant operators to understand why a model triggered an automated in-kernel drop.

blackbox-sentinel incorporates Microsecond Residual Decomposition (MRD), rendering the top-3 physical feature deviations live on the web console within milliseconds of an attack mitigation.
path: Real-Time Explainable AI (XAI) Feature Attribution Viewer

items.title: 1. Microsecond Residual Decomposition (MRD) Architecture
items.text:
Instead of calculating computationally prohibitive SHAP or LIME values (which take seconds to evaluate), the C++ engine computes element-wise autoencoder residuals in \(< 80\,\text{nanoseconds}\):

\[e_j = (x_j - \hat{x}_j)^2\] \[\text{Top-3 Attributions} = \operatorname{arg\,max}_{j \in \{1 \dots D\}} \left(e_j\right)\] 
 [ Model Prediction Anomaly Flagged (Reconstruction MSE > 0.082) ]
                               │
                               ▼ Fast Element-wise Residual Compute (< 80 ns)
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ Semantic Dictionary Attribution Lookup (SemanticDictionary.hpp)
 ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │ #1 Contributor (64%): Modbus Target Register 40001 Overwrite│
 │ #2 Contributor (24%): Flow Packet Rate Deviation (+75k pps) │
 │ #3 Contributor (12%): Abnormal TCP Window Zero-Flagging     │
 └─────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘

items.title: 2. In-Memory Asset Compilation (EmbeddedWebAssets.hpp)
items.text:
Static HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and SVG assets are minified, compressed with gzip, and converted into binary C++ byte arrays during compilation using a custom CMake tool (bin2c):

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>
#include <span>

namespace sentinel::web {

// Statically compiled in-memory compressed assets
extern const uint8_t INDEX_HTML_GZ[];
extern const size_t INDEX_HTML_GZ_LEN;

extern const uint8_t APP_JS_GZ[];
extern const size_t APP_JS_GZ_LEN;

class AssetManager {
public:
    static std::span<const uint8_t> get_asset(std::string_view path, std::string_view& out_mime_type) noexcept {
        if (path == "/" || path == "/index.html") {
            out_mime_type = "text/html; charset=utf-8";
            return {INDEX_HTML_GZ, INDEX_HTML_GZ_LEN};
        }
        if (path == "/app.js") {
            out_mime_type = "application/javascript; charset=utf-8";
            return {APP_JS_GZ, APP_JS_GZ_LEN};
        }
        out_mime_type = "text/plain";
        return {};
    }
};

} // namespace sentinel::web

items.title: ccsds-guard: Autonomous UAV Swarm Tactical Defense & Aerospace Telecommand Engine
items.text:
Deterministic, zero-allocation C++20 validation engine securing autonomous UAV swarms and satellite communications against command replay, GPS-spoofing, and telemetry desynchronization. Complies with NATO STANAG 4586 and CCSDS 133.0-B-2, delivering sliding-window sequence monotonicity checks and actuator air-gaps in < 120 ns (empirically benchmarked at 23.77 ns mean latency).

Engineered by Aryorithm Technologies B.V. (Amsterdam, The Netherlands) as the aerospace & tactical swarm defense vertical of the Blackbox Sentinel cyber-physical defense ecosystem.

items.title: 1. Executive Overview
items.text:
Autonomous Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) swarms and Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite links operate in contested Electronic Warfare (EW) environments where adversaries inject stale telecommand replays, GPS kinematic teleportation spoofing, and clock desynchronization jitter over Software-Defined Radio (SDR) datalinks.

ccsds-guard operates directly in the zero-copy packet ingestion hot-path (std::span<const uint8_t>) prior to flight-controller actuator bus propagation:

  • Zero Dynamic Heap Allocation: 0 bytes allocated (new/malloc) during runtime packet inspection.
  • 128-Bit Cache-Line Aligned Anti-Replay (< 25 ns): Branchless circular bitmask (alignas(64)) enforcing strict sequence monotonicity while tolerating out-of-order radio link jitter within a 128-frame sliding window.
  • NATO STANAG 4586 DLI & IEEE-754 3D Waypoint Unpacking: Bit-level validation of Vehicle ID, Message Type, Sequence Counter, 64-bit Microsecond Epoch Timestamp, and 12-byte IEEE-754 big-endian 3D coordinates (X, Y, Z) via C++20 std::bit_cast<float>.
  • CCSDS 132.0-B-2 & 133.0-B-2 Space Data Link Security: Validates Spacecraft ID (SCID), Virtual Channel ID (VCID), Security Parameter Index (SPI), Anti-Replay IV Counter, and CRC-16-CCITT frame integrity.
  • Dead-Reckoning Kinematic Envelope & Control Barrier Function (\(h(x) \ge 0\)): Evaluates 3D Euclidean trajectory deltas (\(\Delta P / \Delta T\)) against airframe physical velocity (\(\le 80.0\text{ m/s}\)) and structural acceleration (\(\le 30.0\text{ m/s}^2\)) boundaries.
  • Sub-15 ns Hardware Actuator Air-Gap Latch: Immediately isolates downstream PWM/CAN/MAVLink servo lines upon replay, desynchronization, or GPS spoofing detection, placing the airframe into fail-safe aerodynamic glide.

items.title: ICS-GUARD: Sovereign Deterministic OT & SCADA Security Engine
Sub-120 ns Physical Invariant Verification & Active Conduit Defense (IEC 62443 Levels 1–2)
1. Executive Summary & OT Engineering Rationale
items.text:
Standard IT cybersecurity appliances fail in Operational Technology (OT) environments because they optimize for data confidentiality over physical safety and availability. Deep packet inspection engines that introduce non-deterministic buffering (> 5 ms jitter), rely on cloud lookups, or enforce blind TCP resets can trip high-voltage breakers, cause pump cavitation, or induce compressor surges.

ics-guard is a zero-allocation, hardware-rooted cyber-physical security appliance designed for deployment at Purdue Model Levels 1 and 2 (Control Conduits and Industrial LANs).

Operating as an active in-line safety interlock or a non-intrusive optical TAP listener, ics-guard inspects industrial protocol commands at wire speed (11.96 ns mean verification latency), cross-correlating digital network packets with Runge-Kutta 4th-Order (RK4) continuous physical dynamics and formal Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) before malicious setpoints reach physical field actuators.

items.title: 3. Supported Industrial Protocols & Deep Invariant Dissection
items.text: ics-guard implements native C++20 dissectors covering critical industrial infrastructure protocols:

items.title: A. Modbus TCP / IP (Port 502)
items.text:
• MBAP Bounds Checking: Validates Transaction ID, Protocol Identifier (0x0000), Length byte calculation, and Unit ID consistency.
  • Function Code Whitelisting: Enforces read-only policies (FC01 Coils, FC02 Discrete Inputs, FC03 Holding Registers, FC04 Input Registers).
  • Write-Lock & Range Isolation: Intercepts FC05 (Write Single Coil), FC06 (Write Single Register), and FC15/16 (Multiple Write). Blocks writes targeting safety-critical memory ranges (e.g., setpoints in registers 40001–40100).
  • Diagnostic & Smuggling Mitigation: Drops unauthorized diagnostic commands (FC08), encapsulated interface commands (FC2B), and malformed frames used for protocol tunneling.

items.title: B. Siemens S7Comm (Port 102)
items.text:
• TPKT / COTP Framing: Verifies TPKT Version 3 (0x03) and ISO 8073 COTP connection state machine (Connection Request 0xE0, Confirm 0xD0).
  • S7 PDU ROSCTR Inspection: Inspects S7 Comm Protocol Data Unit (0x32), verifying Job Requests (ROSCTR 0x01) and Userdata (ROSCTR 0x07).
  • Stuxnet PLC-State Override Prevention: Detects and drops CPU Control commands targeting PLC mode switches:
  • Blocks CPU STOP (Function 0x29).
  • Blocks Program Invocations (Function 0x28).
  • Blocks unauthorized variable writes (Function 0x05) and block downloads (0x1A..0x1C) targeting Safety Data Blocks (DBs).

items.title: C. IEC 60870-5-104 Telecontrol (Port 2404)
items.text:
• APCI Frame State Machine: Validates Start-Frame 0x68, Length byte, and supervisory frames (U-frames: TESTFR, STARTDT, STOPDT; S-frames: sequence confirmation).
  • ASDU Command Filtering (Industroyer / CrashRAT Mitigation):
  • Dissects Type Identifier commands (Type 45: Single Command, Type 46: Double Command, Type 47: Regulating Step Command, Types 58–64: Time-Tagged Setpoints).
  • Breaker Trip Lockout: Detects Cause of Transmission (COT 6 - Activation / COT 8 - Deactivation) directed at high-voltage transmission substation breakers and triggers line-rate drop.

items.title: D. IEEE C37.118.2 Synchrophasor Power Grid Standards (Port 15501)
items.text:
• Frame Synchronization: Validates IEEE Sync bytes (0xAA) and P/M-class data frames.
  • Frequency Band Enforcement: Monitors high-voltage transmission grid frequency with sub-millihertz precision, enforcing tight grid bounds (49.50 Hz ≤ f ≤ 50.50 Hz).
  • Rate-of-Change-of-Frequency (ROCOF): Clamps transient frequency drift rate (\(|\text{ROCOF}| \le 1.0\,\text{Hz/s}\)) to prevent cascading blackout trips.
  • Total Harmonic Distortion (THD): Inspects 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 5th harmonic spectral energy, triggering alert thresholds when \(\text{THD} > 8.0\%\).

items.title: 4. Physics-Informed Control Theory: Nagumo Control Barrier Functions
items.text:
Pure signature and protocol checks cannot identify an attacker who uses authentic, authorized protocol frames to drive a physical process into catastrophic runaway (e.g., slowly increasing chemical reactor pressure or heating an exothermic catalyst).

ics-guard integrates an embedded Runge-Kutta 4th-Order (RK4) numerical ODE solver and enforces Nagumo Forward Invariance via Control Barrier Functions (CBFs):

\[\mathcal{C} = \{ x \in \mathbb{R}^n \mid h(x) \ge 0 \}\] \[\dot{h}(x, u) + \alpha(h(x)) \ge 0\] 
// Example: Thermal Runway Invariant Check (plant_ode.c)
double plant_cbf_evaluate(const plant_state_t *state, double max_temp_c) {
    // Safe set boundary: h(x) = T_max - T(t) >= 0
    return max_temp_c - state->temperature;
}

bool plant_cbf_check_invariance(const plant_state_t *state, const plant_control_t *control, double max_temp_c, double alpha) {
    double h_val = plant_cbf_evaluate(state, max_temp_c);
    double h_dot_val = plant_cbf_dot_evaluate(state, control);
    // Nagumo invariance: dh/dt + alpha * h(x) >= 0
    return (h_dot_val + alpha * h_val) >= 0.0;
}

If an incoming Modbus or S7 command requests a control input \(u(t)\) that violates the invariance inequality—meaning the physical plant will breach critical operating boundaries within the critical time horizon \(T_\text{crit}\)—the command is dropped immediately at the kernel boundary (ACTUATOR_AIRGAP_TRIPPED), independent of what SCADA or HMI dashboards report.

items.title: MOTION-GUARD: Robotics, Industrial Fieldbus & Autonomous Motion Safety Governor
Sub-120 ns Non-IP EtherCAT (0x88A4), SocketCAN CAN-FD, ShmRing & Nagumo CBF Gate (ISO 13849 PL-e)
1. Executive Summary & Robotics Safety Engineering Scope
items.text:
Industrial articulated robots, collaborative workcells (cobots), autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), and heavy mining haul trucks operate within physical spaces shared with human workers and multi-ton payloads. In these systems, standard software firewalls cannot prevent mechanical disasters:

  1. Non-IP Fieldbus Vulnerability: Real-time servo controllers and robotic joints communicate over EtherCAT (0x88A4) or CAN-FD, which do not use IP addresses, TCP, or UDP. Traditional firewalls cannot inspect or filter these packets.
  2. Kinematic & Control Surges: An attacker or rogue trajectory planner commanding an acceleration of \(48\,\text{m/s}^2\) on a \(500\,\text{kg}\) robotic arm will shear gearboxes or breach safety fences before an operator can reach an E-stop button.
  3. Sensor-Fusion Blindness: Autonomous mining haul trucks and AGVs can suffer steering hijacking or obstacle-sensor freezing. Without cross-validation between the fieldbus actuation conduit and physical obstacle boundaries, high-speed collisions occur.

motion-guard is the robotics and motion safety vertical for the Aryorithm Sentinel Ecosystem. Designed to comply with ISO 13849-1 Performance Level e (PL-e) and ISO/TS 15066, it combines a zero-allocation C++20 Tier-1 deterministic protocol dissector with formal Nagumo Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) and three multi-bus ingress adapters:

items.title: 2. Formal Control Theory: Nagumo Control Barrier Functions
items.text:
Rather than relying purely on static heuristics, motion-guard models physical kinetic boundaries mathematically using Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) and guarantees safety forward-invariance under Nagumo's theorem:

Given a safe operating set \(\mathcal{C}\):

\[\mathcal{C} = \left\{ x \in \mathbb{R}^n \;\middle|\; h_v(x) = v_{\max} - |v| \ge 0 \right\}\]

The system is safe for all forward time \(t \ge 0\) if and only if the control input satisfies:

\[\dot{h}_v(x, u) + \alpha \cdot h_v(x) \ge 0\]

Where: * \(v\) is the measured joint or vehicle velocity. * \(\dot{h}_v = -\text{sgn}(v) \cdot a\) (derived from acceleration \(a = \dot{v}\)). * \(\alpha > 0\) is the class-\(\mathcal{K}\) convergence parameter (default: \(\alpha = 4.0\)).

// Formal Nagumo Velocity Invariance Verification (motion_cbf_gate.cpp)
GuardStatus MotionCbfGate::evaluate(const MotionState& state, const MotionCbfLimits& limits) noexcept {
    // 1. Strict kinematic envelope checks
    if (std::abs(state.position_mm) > limits.max_position_mm ||
        std::abs(state.torque_nm) > limits.max_torque_nm) {
        return GuardStatus::REJECT_CBF_BOUNDARY_BREACH;
    }

    // 2. Control Barrier Function calculation: h_v(x) = v_max - |v| >= 0
    const double h_v = limits.max_velocity_mps - std::abs(state.velocity_mps);
    const double sign_v = (state.velocity_mps >= 0.0) ? 1.0 : -1.0;
    const double h_v_dot = -sign_v * state.accel_mps2;

    // 3. Nagumo forward invariance inequality: dh/dt + alpha * h(x) >= 0
    if (h_v < 0.0 || (h_v_dot + limits.nagumo_alpha * h_v) < 0.0) {
        return GuardStatus::REJECT_CBF_BOUNDARY_BREACH;
    }

    return GuardStatus::PASS;
}

If a trajectory command breaches this boundary, motion-guard drops the packet in under \(120\,\text{ns}\), tripping the hardware safety air-gap latch (MOTION_AIRGAP_TRIPPED) before mechanical damage can occur.

items.title: A. Bus A: Non-IP Layer-2 EtherCAT (EtherType 0x88A4)
items.text:
• Physical Framing: Ingests raw Ethernet frames directly via AF_PACKET raw sockets without an IPv4/TCP stack.
  • PDU Header Parsing: Decodes the 2-byte EtherCAT header (Length lower 11 bits, Type upper 4 bits where Type == 1).
  • PDO Joint Acceleration Validation: Extracts 8-byte Process Data Objects (PDO) representing floating-point joint acceleration (\(a\)) and tool center point (TCP) workspace radius (\(R\)).
  • Enforces maximum allowable collaborative acceleration (\(|a| \le 15.0\,\text{m/s}^2\)).
  • Enforces maximum workspace reach (\(R \le 850.0\,\text{mm}\)) to prevent fence breaches.
  • Working Counter (WKC) Anti-Tamper: Validates that slave node Working Counters match the expected physical topology count (\(\text{WKC} \ge 1\)). Drops packets indicating injected or dropped slave frames (REJECT_ETHERCAT_WKC_TAMPER).

items.title: B. Bus B: Fieldbus CAN / CAN-FD (SocketCAN / can://bus0)
items.text:
• Framing: Ingests standard Linux struct can_frame (16 bytes) and struct canfd_frame (up to 64 bytes).
  • Arbitration ID Allowlist: Enforces permitted J1939 / CANopen message IDs (0x100 ≤ ID ≤ 0x5FF). Rejects unauthorized diagnostic or reflashing frames such as 0x7DF (REJECT_CAN_UNAUTHORIZED_ID).
  • Drive-by-Wire Steering & Torque Boundaries:
  • Evaluates 32-bit floating-point steering angles at byte offset 8. Clamps maximum steering authority (\(|\theta_{\text{steer}}| \le 35.0^\circ\)) to prevent high-speed rollover attacks on mining haul trucks (REJECT_CAN_ACTUATOR_OVERRIDE).
  • Clamps drive motor torque commands (\(|\tau| \le 250.0\,\text{Nm}\)).

items.title: C. Bus C: Direct Memory POSIX Shared Memory Ring (shm://ring0)
items.text:
• Memory Architecture: Uses POSIX shm_open() with 4KB page alignment inside Docker (ipc: shareable) or host memory.
  • Header Magic: Validates 4-byte identifier 0x4D4F5431 ("MOT1").
  • AMR LiDAR Collision Interlock: Cross-correlates mobile robot velocity (\(v\)) with forward minimum obstacle range (\(d_{\text{obs}}\)).
  • Forces an immediate emergency stop if velocity is active (\(|v| > 0.2\,\text{m/s}\)) and clearance is breached (\(d_{\text{obs}} < 0.50\,\text{m}\)) (REJECT_SHM_OBSTACLE_COLLISION).

Sub-120 ns Non-IP Layer-2 GOOSE, 3GPP GTP-U Slicing, ITCH 5.0 Pre-Trade & PQC Gate
1. Executive Summary & Systems Engineering Scope
items.text:
Modern high-velocity network infrastructure operates under extreme throughput and timing constraints where traditional IP firewalls create unacceptable buffer bloat, microsecond jitter, and protocol blind spots:

  1. 5G / Private Network Slicing: A User Plane Function (UPF) must enforce strict multi-tenant tenant isolation across Ultra-Reliable Low-Latency Communication (URLLC) and enhanced Mobile Broadband (eMBB) slices without adding packet latency to autonomous robotics or telesurgery.
  2. Substation Digital Busbars (Non-IP Layer 2): High-voltage electrical substations communicate critical protection trips over raw Ethernet multicast frames (IEC 61850 GOOSE 0x88B8 and Sampled Values 0x88BA). Traditional Layer-3/4 firewalls discard these frames entirely because they contain no IP or TCP/UDP headers.
  3. FinTech High-Frequency Trading (HFT): Exchange gateways and algorithmic order routers must evaluate risk parameters (fat-finger share caps, price collars) at sub-microsecond wire speed to satisfy SEC Rule 15c3-5 without compromising trade execution queues.
  4. Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) Transition: Critical conduits must detect and block "Harvest-Now, Decrypt-Later" downgrades to classical cipher suites by enforcing NIST ML-KEM key encapsulation in raw TLS 1.3 handshakes.

net-guard is the high-speed wire vertical for the Aryorithm Sentinel Ecosystem. Compiled as a zero-allocation, lock-free C++20 engine linked to blackbox-sentinel and xinfer-essential, it leverages Linux AF_PACKET raw sockets, AF_XDP kernel bypass, and hardware cycle-accurate TSC timers to enforce deterministic inspection at \(< 120\,\text{ns}\) latency.

items.title: A. 3GPP 5G UPF GTPv1-U Protocol (UDP Port 2152)
items.text:
• Standards: 3GPP TS 29.281, 3GPP TS 23.501 (5G System Architecture).
  • Header Validation: Enforces GTPv1 flags (Version == 1, Protocol Type == 1), Message Type (0xFF G-PDU), and optional Extension Header padding.
  • Tunnel Endpoint Identifier (TEID) Slicing:
  • Maps 32-bit TEID ranges to Network Slices: URLLC (0x00000100–0x000001FF) vs. eMBB (0x00000200–0x000002FF).
  • Slice-Hopping Interception: Performs wire-speed decapsulation of the inner IPv4 packet inside the G-PDU payload. If an eMBB user terminal sends packets targeting restricted operational control ports (502 Modbus, 102 S7, 2404 IEC-104), net-guard drops the packet instantly (REJECT_GTPU_SLICE_HOPPING).
  • Unauthorized TEID drop (REJECT_GTPU_UNAUTHORIZED_TEID).

items.title: B. Non-IP Layer-2 IEC 61850 GOOSE & Sampled Values (0x88B8 / 0x88BA)
items.text:
• Standards: IEC 61850-8-1 (Specific Communication Service Mapping for GOOSE), IEC 61850-9-2 (Sampled Values).
  • Ingress Mechanism: Linux AF_PACKET raw socket capturing directly from Ethernet MAC without IP stack overhead.
  • APPID & PDU Verification:
  • Enforces valid IEEE APPID allocation: GOOSE (0x0000 ≤ APPID ≤ 0x3FFF), Sampled Values (0x4000 ≤ APPID ≤ 0x7FFF).
  • State Number (stNum) Anti-Spoof: Enforces monotonic forward progression of breaker trip state numbers (stNum). Replayed packets with stale or decrementing stNum counters are dropped (REJECT_GOOSE_SPOOFED_STNUM).
  • Sequence Number (sqNum) Heartbeat Audit: Validates message burst intervals during protection trip events.

items.title: C. FinTech NASDAQ ITCH 5.0 & OUCH Pre-Trade Protocol (TCP Port 9001)
items.text:
• Standards: NASDAQ TotalView-ITCH 5.0, NASDAQ OUCH 5.0, SEC Rule 15c3-5.
  • Pre-Trade Risk Collar Gate:
  • Ingests Add Order messages ('A', 'F') and Enter Order messages ('O').
  • Fat-Finger Quantity Clamp: Reads 32-bit big-endian share quantities at byte offset 20. Orders exceeding client margin policy (e.g. \(> 10,000\) shares) are intercepted in under \(15\,\text{ns}\) before hitting the matching engine (REJECT_ITCH_FAT_FINGER_QTY).
  • Price Collar Band: Evaluates 32-bit \(10^{-4}\) scaled prices at byte offset 32. Rejects orders outside exchange circuit-breaker collars (REJECT_ITCH_PRICE_COLLAR).

items.title: D. O-RAN Near-RT RIC E2AP Protocol (SCTP Port 36422)
items.text:
• Standards: O-RAN Alliance WG3 E2AP Specification v03.00.
  • xApp Sandboxing Interlock:
  • Inspects E2AP Elementary Procedures transmitted over Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP).
  • Permits telemetry observation (RICindication, Procedure Code 5).
  • Intercepts rogue or uncertified xApp actuation commands attempting radio beamforming or slice-bandwidth mutation (RICcontrol, Procedure Code 4; E2nodeConfigurationUpdate, Procedure Code 10) unless explicitly authorized (REJECT_ORAN_ROGUE_XAPP_CONTROL).

  • Drops connections attempting classical-only Elliptic Curve downgrades (secp256r1, x25519) on mission-critical banking and defense conduits (REJECT_PQC_CLASSICAL_DOWNGRADE).

Every .spkg is a deterministic binary container with the following layout:

+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| 5. SECTION 3: AUDITABLE PLAIN-TEXT SOURCE CODE                                                     |
|    • Raw `src/lib.rs`, `src/plugin.cpp`, or `rule.lua` stored directly inside the container        |
|    • Allows air-gapped industrial regulators (IEC 62443 / CMMC) to audit logic without Git        |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

items.title: 6.1 Package Toolchain: sentinel-spkg
items.text:
The sentinel-spkg utility (built in blackbox-sentinel/build/sentinel-spkg) manages package authoring:

# 1. Scaffold a new Rust WebAssembly package
sentinel-spkg new s7_power_guard rust

# 2. Generate a certified Ed25519 developer keypair
sentinel-spkg keygen operator_key

# 3. Compile the Rust code
cd s7_power_guard && cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --release && cd ..

# 4. Pack all 4 sections into a sealed .spkg container
sentinel-spkg pack operator_key_private.pem 1 \
    s7_power_guard/manifest.json \
    s7_power_guard/target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/s7_power_guard.wasm \
    s7_power_guard/src/lib.rs \
    s7_power_guard/tests/preflight_frame.bin \
    dist/s7_power_guard.spkg

# 5. Inspect container metadata, source size, and latency SLA
sentinel-spkg inspect dist/s7_power_guard.spkg

# 6. Verify cryptographic Merkle signature
sentinel-spkg verify operator_key_public.pem dist/s7_power_guard.spkg

sentinel-spkg extract-source dist/s7_power_guard.spkg /tmp/auditor_review.rs

It transforms cybersecurity research from slow, static CSV/PCAP offline analysis into an air-gapped, hardware-aware, closed-loop cyber-physical evaluation suite.

Designed for systems researchers, defense engineers, and university labs, sentinel-lab provides a 14-dimension scientific research suite capable of evaluating real-time worst-case execution time (WCET) determinism, CPU microarchitecture cache miss rates, closed-loop physical plant differential equations, formal control barrier functions, SCADA request smuggling zero-days, post-quantum cryptography (PQC) overheads, and multi-silicon quantization drift—without requiring million-euro physical SCADA testbed hardware.

items.title: 3. Binary Wire Format: The SLAB Protocol (0x534C4142)
items.text: To achieve wire-speed transmission (\(> 60{,}000\text{ EPS}\)) over Linux raw sockets (AF_PACKET / SOCK_RAW) without serialization overhead, sentinel-lab utilizes the SLAB Binary Wire Protocol.

items.title: Packed 24-Byte Header Specification
items.text:
#pragma once
#include <cstdint>

namespace sentinel::lab {

inline constexpr uint32_t SLAB_MAGIC = 0x534C4142; // ASCII: 'S', 'L', 'A', 'B'

#pragma pack(push, 1)
struct SlabHeader {
    uint32_t magic;          // Byte 0-3  : 0x534C4142
    uint64_t event_id;       // Byte 4-11 : Monotonic sequence identifier
    uint32_t ground_truth;   // Byte 12-15: 0 = Benign, 1 = Attack
    uint32_t dimensions;     // Byte 16-19: Feature count D (1 .. 1024)
    uint32_t flags;          // Byte 20-23: Bitmask flags / Reserved
};
#pragma pack(pop)

static_assert(sizeof(SlabHeader) == 24, "SlabHeader must be exactly 24 bytes");

} // namespace sentinel::lab
  • Wire Frame Layout: [ 24-Byte SlabHeader ] + [ D * 4-Byte IEEE 754 Float32 Tensor Payload ]
  • Zero-Copy Handshake: DimensionHandshake::extract_features() reinterpret-casts memory buffers into zero-copy std::span<const float> views without heap allocation.

items.title: Executive Academic Overview
items.text:
sentinel-lab is an open-source, peer-reviewed scientific evaluation platform and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) research testbed. It resolves the widespread reproducibility crisis in cyber-physical intrusion detection research, where academic papers evaluate machine learning models on static, offline CSV files without testing live packet injection, bus latencies, or kernel drop mechanics.

Operating over raw Linux network sockets (AF_PACKET), sentinel-lab introduces the SLAB Universal Binary Wire Protocol, streams the official Canadian Institute for Cybersecurity CIC-IDS-2017 PortScan benchmark dataset at line rate (\(> 60{,}000\text{ EPS}\)), and benchmarks heterogeneous edge AI inference engines (Intel OpenVINO NPU vs. NVIDIA TensorRT) against Linux in-kernel eBPF/XDP drop filters.

items.title: Core Invariants
items.text:
1. Deterministic Reproducibility: Every empirical table, confusion matrix, and latency percentile published in the IEEE preprint paper can be regenerated locally using a single command: python3 examples/run_full_evaluation.py.
  2. Hardware-in-the-Loop Realism: Moves beyond theoretical Python notebooks; models evaluate live, streaming binary frames passing over real Linux network sockets.
  3. Open-Access Scientific Attribution: Released under permissive dual licensing (MIT License for code; Creative Commons CC-BY-4.0 for data, benchmark traces, and LaTeX manuscripts) with a permanent CERN/Zenodo DOI.
  4. Cross-Architecture Equity: Evaluates Intel, NVIDIA, and ARM silicon targets under identical batch constraints (\(N=1\)), identical memory isolation, and identical microsecond measurement harnesses.

items.title: The Academic Reproducibility Crisis in Network Security
items.text:
Over \(85\%\) of published academic papers in machine learning-based network intrusion detection evaluate models using offline CSV datasets (e.g., loading KDDCup99, NSL-KDD, or CIC-IDS-2017 into a Python Jupyter Notebook with Pandas and Scikit-Learn).

This methodology introduces what sentinel-lab defines as the "CSV Illusion".

items.title: 2. Why Offline CSV Training Fails in Production
items.text:
1. Feature Extraction Latency is Ignored: In static CSVs, statistical features (e.g., Flow Duration, Fwd Packet Length StdDev) are already calculated. On a real \(10\text{ GbE}\) network, extracting these statistics in user-space consumes hundreds of microseconds—far exceeding line-rate budgets.
  2. Missing System Latencies: An offline model does not account for kernel interrupt handling, softirq NAPI poll loops, socket buffer allocation (sk_buff), or bus contention.
  3. No Active Mitigation Proof: Predicting an attack in a notebook provides zero proof that the host operating system can drop the packet before application compromise occurs.

sentinel-lab eliminates this disparity by evaluating models on live, streaming network frames under realistic line-rate pressure.

items.title: Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) Testbed Design
items.text: sentinel-lab bridges theoretical algorithms and physical network hardware using a Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) architecture.

items.title: 2. Invariants of the HIL Methodology
items.text:
• Live Line-Rate Ingestion: Traffic is transmitted over physical network interface cards (e.g., Intel X520 10GbE or E810 25GbE) rather than software mock queues.
  • Driver-Level Packet Drops: Verified by observing the physical hardware drop counters (ethtool -S eth0 | grep rx_dropped) on the network controller.
  • Silicon Isolation: AI models run directly on physical acceleration coprocessors (Intel Neural Processing Units, NVIDIA Tensor Cores) subjected to real-world PCIe bus transfers.

items.title: Microsecond Clock Precision & Latency Measurement Physics
items.text:
Measuring end-to-end latencies below \(1.0\,\mu\text{s}\) requires nanosecond-level instrumentation. Standard operating system calls—such as gettimeofday() or std::chrono::system_clock—introduce measurement overhead (\(15 - 30\,\text{ns}\)) and are subject to NTP adjustments.

sentinel-lab uses hardware-level timestamping and CPU cycle counters.

items.title: 2. Serialized Cycle Reading Implementation
items.text:
Standard __rdtsc instructions can be executed out-of-order by speculative CPU execution pipelines. sentinel-lab uses instruction-fenced cycle reading:

#include <cstdint>

namespace sentinel::lab {

[[nodiscard]] inline uint64_t read_invariant_tsc() noexcept {
    uint32_t low, high;
    // The rdtscp instruction waits until all previous instructions have executed,
    // ensuring speculative execution does not distort the timing window.
    asm volatile("rdtscp" : "=a"(low), "=d"(high) : : "rcx");
    return (static_cast<uint64_t>(high) << 32) | low;
}

[[nodiscard]] inline double cycles_to_microseconds(uint64_t cycles, double cpu_ghz) noexcept {
    // Latency (µs) = Cycles / (CPU_Freq_GHz * 1000)
    return static_cast<double>(cycles) / (cpu_ghz * 1000.0);
}

} // namespace sentinel::lab

items.title: 2. Low-Latency Socket Polling Loop (src/engine/polling_loop.cpp)
items.text:
To avoid OS scheduler latency, sentinel_lab operates a dedicated busy-polling thread pinned to an isolated CPU core:

#include <sys/socket.h>
#include <linux/if_packet.h>
#include <net/ethernet.h>
#include <sentinel_lab/slab_protocol.hpp>
#include <sentinel_lab/metrics.hpp>
#include <xinfer/xinfer.hpp>

namespace sentinel::lab {

void run_benchmark_polling_loop(
    int raw_sock_fd, 
    xinfer::InferenceEngine& ai_engine, 
    ScientificMetrics& metrics,
    std::atomic<bool>& keep_running
) {
    alignas(64) uint8_t packet_buffer[2048];

    while (keep_running.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)) {
        // 1. Non-blocking packet reception from raw socket
        ssize_t bytes_received = ::recv(raw_sock_fd, packet_buffer, sizeof(packet_buffer), MSG_DONTWAIT);
        if (bytes_received <= 0) {
            continue; // Busy-poll: zero thread sleep to avoid scheduler jitter
        }

        // 2. Hardware Timer: Ingress Mark
        uint64_t t_ingress = read_invariant_tsc();

        // 3. Zero-Copy Header Cast
        if (bytes_received < sizeof(SlabHeader)) continue;
        const auto* slab = reinterpret_cast<const SlabHeader*>(packet_buffer);

        if (slab->magic != SLAB_MAGIC) continue; // Skip non-SLAB frames

        // 4. Map continuous float tensor view (Skipping 24-byte SLAB header)
        const float* tensor_data = reinterpret_cast<const float*>(packet_buffer + sizeof(SlabHeader));
        std::span<const float> input_features(tensor_data, slab->dimensions);

        // 5. Execute Neural Forward Pass
        auto input_tensor = ai_engine.get_input_tensor(0);
        input_tensor->copy_from_host(input_features.data(), input_features.size_bytes());
        ai_engine.forward();

        // 6. Hardware Timer: Egress / Mitigation Mark
        uint64_t t_mitigated = read_invariant_tsc();
        uint64_t delta_cycles = t_mitigated - t_ingress;

        // 7. Update Classification & Latency Metrics
        float prediction = *ai_engine.get_output_tensor(0)->data<float>();
        metrics.record_event(slab->ground_truth, prediction > 0.5f, delta_cycles);
    }
}

} // namespace sentinel::lab

items.title: Zero-Overhead Performance Instrumentation
items.text:
In low-latency systems research, profiling latency can alter execution behavior (the "Observer Effect"). Logging timestamps via dynamic allocations or locks introduces latency spikes that corrupt high-percentile distributions (\(p99\) and \(p99.9\)).

sentinel-lab utilizes Zero-Overhead Static Instrumentation.

items.title: 1. Pre-Allocated Logarithmic Histogram Bins
items.text:
Instead of recording every raw timestamp into dynamically resizing vectors, execution latencies are sorted in-place into pre-allocated logarithmic histogram bins:

#include <array>
#include <atomic>
#include <cstdint>

namespace sentinel::lab {

class LatencyHistogram {
public:
    static constexpr size_t NUM_BINS = 1024;
    static constexpr uint64_t BIN_WIDTH_NS = 10; // 10ns resolution per bin

    void record_latency(uint64_t latency_ns) noexcept {
        size_t bin = latency_ns / BIN_WIDTH_NS;
        if (bin >= NUM_BINS) {
            bin = NUM_BINS - 1; // Cap at max overflow bin (10.24 µs)
        }
        bins_[bin].fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    }

    [[nodiscard]] double calculate_percentile(double percentile) const {
        // Post-processing executed after benchmark completion
        uint64_t total = 0;
        for (const auto& b : bins_) total += b.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);

        uint64_t target = static_cast<uint64_t>(total * (percentile / 100.0));
        uint64_t accumulated = 0;

        for (size_t i = 0; i < NUM_BINS; ++i) {
            accumulated += bins_[i].load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
            if (accumulated >= target) {
                return static_cast<double>(i * BIN_WIDTH_NS) / 1000.0; // Return in µs
            }
        }
        return static_cast<double>(NUM_BINS * BIN_WIDTH_NS) / 1000.0;
    }

private:
    std::array<std::atomic<uint64_t>, NUM_BINS> bins_{};
};

} // namespace sentinel::lab

items.title: 2. Invariants
items.text:
• \(O(1)\) Execution Cost: Binned recording executes in under 4 CPU cycles (\(\approx 1.2\,\text{ns}\)).
  • Zero Mutex Contention: Atomic relaxation (memory_order_relaxed) ensures worker threads do not stall when updating metrics.
  • Cache Isolation: Histogram bins reside in contiguous, pre-warmed memory pages, eliminating Level 3 cache eviction during benchmark runs.

items.title: Comparative Analysis: Sentinel-Lab vs. Suricata 7.0
items.text: Suricata is widely adopted in enterprise and academic networks. In active prevention mode, Suricata relies on the Linux Netfilter queue (NFQUEUE) to inspect packets in user space and issue drop verdicts.

 Suricata 7.0 (NFQUEUE Inline) : ════════════════════════════════ 8,400.0 µs (8.4 ms)

items.text: Metric Suricata 7.0 (NFQUEUE Inline) sentinel-lab (In-Kernel eBPF/XDP) Advantage Factor Mitigation Latency (\(p50\)) \(8{,}400.0\,\mu\text{s}\) (\(8.4\,\text{ms}\)) \(0.72\,\mu\text{s}\) (\(720\,\text{ns}\)) \(11{,}666\times\) Faster Mitigation Latency (\(p99\)) \(14{,}800.0\,\mu\text{s}\) (\(14.8\,\text{ms}\)) \(0.84\,\mu\text{s}\) (\(840\,\text{ns}\)) \(17{,}619\times\) Faster Max Inline Throughput \(420{,}000\text{ pps}\) (Per Core) \(14{,}880{,}000\text{ pps}\) (Line Rate) \(35.4\times\) Higher Memory Buffer Footprint \(1{,}850\text{ MB}\) (Rule Trees) \(32\text{ MB}\) (Pinned BPF Maps) \(57\times\) Leaner Socket Buffer Allocation Requires alloc_skb() Zero sk_buff Allocations Eliminates Slab Locks

items.title: 2. Why Suricata Incurs Millisecond Delays
items.text:
1. Netlink Serialization Overhead: Every packet must be copied from the kernel ring through Netlink socket buffers into user space.
  2. Context-Switch Latency: Passing execution between kernel interrupt handlers and Suricata’s thread pool incurs heavy scheduling penalties (\(1.5 - 4.5\,\mu\text{s}\) per switch).
  3. Queue Backup Under Load: At line rate, user-space queues overflow, inducing multi-millisecond buffer latency before packet inspection begins.

items.title: Cross-Silicon Normalization Standards & Benchmarking Rules
items.text: To ensure academic validity under peer-review standards, sentinel-lab enforces six benchmarking rules across all silicon evaluations.

items.title: 1. The Six Normalization Rules
items.text: Rule Number Mandate Technical Enforcement Rule 1 Batch Size Invariant (\(N=1\)) All latency percentiles must be recorded with batch size \(1\). Large batches (\(N \ge 64\)) are prohibited for fast-path claims. Rule 2 Precision Normalization Models must be evaluated under matched precisions: INT8 (Quantized Post-Training) or FP16 (Half Precision). Rule 3 Memory Boundary Transparency Timing must encompass host-to-device bus transfer, kernel execution, and device-to-host readback. Rule 4 CPU Core Shielding Execution threads must be pinned to isolated CPU cores excluded from OS scheduling via isolcpus. Rule 5 Cache Pre-Warming Runtimes must execute a minimum of \(10{,}000\) warm-up inferences before recording data. Rule 6 Sample Size Uniformity All cumulative distribution functions (CDF) must record a minimum of \(N = 50{,}000\) continuous evaluations.

items.title: 2. Eliminating Python Jitter
items.text:
In many academic papers, Python garbage collection or global interpreter lock (GIL) contention introduces latency spikes of \(500 - 2000\,\mu\text{s}\).

sentinel-lab benchmarks run entirely in compiled ISO C++20, eliminating runtime garbage collection pauses and ensuring measurement reproducibility.

items.title: 1. Zero-Copy ov::Tensor Memory Mapping
items.text:
To prevent memory copying between the SLAB raw socket receiver and the OpenVINO execution context, sentinel-lab wraps host memory directly into ov::Tensor handles:

#include <openvino/openvino.hpp>
#include <sentinel_lab/slab_protocol.hpp>

namespace sentinel::lab {

class OpenVinoBenchEngine {
public:
    OpenVinoBenchEngine(const std::string& model_path, const std::string& device_name) {
        // device_name: "NPU" or "CPU"
        ov::Core core;

        // Compile model with latency optimization hint
        auto model = core.read_model(model_path);
        compiled_model_ = core.compile_model(model, device_name, 
            ov::hint::performance_mode(ov::hint::PerformanceMode::LATENCY),
            ov::hint::num_requests(1));

        infer_request_ = compiled_model_.create_infer_request();
    }

    double evaluate_slab_frame(const float* raw_features, size_t dim) {
        // Zero-copy pointer wrap: ov::Tensor aliases external host memory
        ov::Shape input_shape = {1, dim};
        ov::Tensor input_tensor(ov::element::f32, input_shape, const_cast<float*>(raw_features));

        infer_request_.set_input_tensor(input_tensor);

        uint64_t t_start = read_invariant_tsc();
        infer_request_.infer(); // Synchronous execution
        uint64_t t_end = read_invariant_tsc();

        return cycles_to_microseconds(t_end - t_start, 3.8); // 3.8 GHz clock
    }

private:
    ov::CompiledModel compiled_model_;
    ov::InferRequest infer_request_;
};

} // namespace sentinel::lab

items.title: 2. C++20 TensorRT Execution Harness
items.text:
#include <NvInfer.h>
#include <cuda_runtime.h>
#include <sentinel_lab/slab_protocol.hpp>

namespace sentinel::lab {

class TensorRtBenchEngine {
public:
    TensorRtBenchEngine(nvinfer1::IExecutionContext* context, cudaStream_t stream)
        : context_(context), stream_(stream) {

        // Allocate pinned host buffers accessible by GPU DMA engine
        cudaHostAlloc(&pinned_input_buffer_, 32 * sizeof(float), cudaHostAllocMapped);
        cudaHostAlloc(&pinned_output_buffer_, 32 * sizeof(float), cudaHostAllocMapped);

        cudaHostGetDevicePointer(&d_input_, pinned_input_buffer_, 0);
        cudaHostGetDevicePointer(&d_output_, pinned_output_buffer_, 0);
    }

    double evaluate_slab_frame(const float* raw_features, size_t dim) {
        // Copy flow features into host-pinned RAM
        std::memcpy(pinned_input_buffer_, raw_features, dim * sizeof(float));

        uint64_t t_start = read_invariant_tsc();

        // Bind memory pointers to TensorRT input/output ports
        context_->setInputTensorAddress("flow_features", d_input_);
        context_->setOutputTensorAddress("reconstruction", d_output_);

        // Enqueue asynchronous inference
        context_->enqueueV3(stream_);
        cudaStreamSynchronize(stream_);

        uint64_t t_end = read_invariant_tsc();
        return cycles_to_microseconds(t_end - t_start, 2.0);
    }

private:

items.title: Thermal & Power Consumption Profiling (Joules per Classification)

In industrial field hardware, edge devices operate under strict power and thermal budgets. Evaluating models solely by inference speed ignores energy efficiency.

sentinel-lab benchmarks silicon efficiency using Energy per Classification (\(J/\text{inf}\)).

items.title: 1. Energy Calculation Formula
items.text:
Instantaneous active power (\(P(t)\) in Watts) is sampled via hardware current sensors throughout a continuous 50,000-packet saturation benchmark:

\[\text{Energy per Inference (Joules)} = \frac{\int_{0}^{T} P_{\text{active}}(t)\, dt}{N_{\text{total}}}\] \[\text{Efficiency} = \frac{\text{Classifications}}{1.0\,\text{Joule}} = \frac{1}{\text{Energy per Inference}}\]
